title: JSON Minifier
description: Minify JSON by parsing it and writing it back without extra spaces. Invalid JSON is reported instead of silently corrupted. Everything stays in the browser.
intro: Paste a JSON document to strip insignificant whitespace. The minifier parses first, so comments are rejected and strings keep their escaped characters.
blurb: Compact valid JSON by removing insignificant whitespace after a real parse.
howItWorks: Paste JSON. Trailing commas and comments are not valid JSON and will be flagged.
Press Minify JSON. The page parses the document, then serializes it with no added spaces.
Compare character counts to see how much formatting whitespace was removed.
examples: A trailing comma such as {"a":1,} is reported as invalid.
Strings keep internal spaces; only structural whitespace is removed.

faq.q: Is this the same as a JSON formatter?
faq.a: A formatter adds indentation for reading. This tool removes that formatting so the document is smaller to paste into configs, query strings or fixtures.
Keys stay in the order the parser returned them, which in current browsers is the order they appeared in the object.
No. Parsing and serialization happen locally with JSON.parse and JSON.stringify.
